overall: Temperatures peaked at 95.0°F around 13:25 ET before severe thunderstorm activity caused dramatic convective cooling — dropping from ~93°F at 12:52 ET to ~79°F by 14:52 ET, with only a partial recovery to 80.6°F by 15:52 ET. This afternoon's storm complex (Severe Thunderstorm Warning with 60 mph gusts north of Cartersville) drove the sharp temperature collapse, leaving the day tracking cooler than the bullish GFS/ECMWF guidance and closer to the more conservative HRRR/NBM models. With roughly 1-2 hours of heating potential remaining, a recovery of the ~14.4°F needed to beat the current running max is extremely unlikely.
forecast_obs_notes: Model spread was wide today — GFS (98.1°F) and ECMWF (96.7°F) were significantly more bullish than HRRR (92.9°F) and NBM (93.6°F); the higher-resolution models better anticipated the convective disruption that truncated afternoon heating. The observed peak of 95.0°F landed above HRRR/NBM but well below GFS/ECMWF, while the META bucket distribution (which still skews toward 98-99°F at 39%) appears to be lagging the intraday reality captured by the give-up classifier (88% fired at hour 13.58).
max_temp_prediction: The daily high of 95.0°F is very likely already set. The give-up classifier fired at 88% confidence, the intraday model assigns 62.5% probability to the 94-95°F bucket, and the steep convective cooling leaves no realistic pathway to surpassing the running max with only late-afternoon hours remaining. For the active even-bucket Kalshi market, the outcome almost certainly falls in the 94-95°F bucket — notably one bucket below the market's top offering of 96-97°F — suggesting the market is currently mispriced toward warmer outcomes. Confidence is high given the locked running max and elapsed peak timing.
